To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pyramidal cell dendritic and axonal growth, spine growth and pruning, and intrinsic membrane properties are differentially expressed in the different cortical regions, and that the expression of these properties varies over time in a region-specific manner.

“the anatomical and electropysiological properties of neocortial pyramidal cells diverge during postnatal development and into adulthood, with some cells pruning spines and others growing spines, and some cells consolidating their intrinsic axons and others pruning their intrinsic axons.”

the dendritic, spine and axon development, as well as the electrophysiology, of neocortial pyramidal cells varies among cortical areas at the time of birth, and continues to diverge over the course of postnatal development.

the anatomical and functional development of pyramidal neurons in the neocortex of the primate brain.

cortical pyramidal cells are not “all the same” and that their development varies across cortical areas.

the anatomical, physiological and behavioral properties of cortical neurons are highly variable across cortical areas and that these variations may be critical for the development and maintenance of the diverse cognitive and behavioral capacities that are unique to primates.
